newsitem.title: UK: H.Young to buy into bikes, sets 116p rights.
newsitem.headline: H.Young to buy into bikes, sets 116p rights.

text.p: British marketing and distribution company H Young Holdings Plc said on Monday it planned to buy venture-capital backed bicycle specialist Madison for 6.86 million stg and would make a share placing and one-for-three rights issue at 116 pence per share.
In a statement, H Young said it was also reporting a 30 percent rise in full-year pre-tax profits to 2.6 million stg and sales up by 12 percent to 56.9 million stg.
Madison, which specialises in the import and distribution of niche bicycle parts and accessories, including to manufacturers, has its main contract with Japanese gear maker Shimano.
Up to now H Young has specialised in branded consumer goods mainly in the optical, automotive and sports sectors, as well as an electronics business directed at commercial clients.
"The board is confident that H Young's financial strength and management skills will enhance Madison's growth prospects," the company said in a statement.
Due to the size of the deal in relation to the company, H Young shareholders will be asked to approve the takeover and share issue at an extraordionary meeting set for December 27.

Under the plans for the transaction, H Young plans to fund about 5.78 million stg, the bulk of the cash element of the purchase, from the share placing and offer. A further 0.47 million stg will be paid from its own cash resources.
The non-cash balance of the purchase price will be paid in loan notes and consideration shares.
H Young proposed a final dividend of 2.9 pence, giving a total for the year of 4.2 pence, up from last year's 3.9 pence.
